title: Scout: Open-World Species Recognition on the Edge
abstract: arXiv:2609.22897v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large vision-language models (VLMs) enable recognition beyond a fixed class set, but their computational demands prevent them from running on many edge devices. Cloud offload makes this capability accessible, but sending every image consumes scarce bandwidth and communication energy. We ask how to bring the open-world recognition capability of VLMs to the edge while operating within tight compute, energy, and bandwidth budgets. Wildlife monitoring provides a natural setting for exploring this question because camera traps encounter species not known at deployment. We present Scout, an autonomous open-world recognition system that invokes a cloud VLM intermittently to teach new classes to a compact edge model. translated_title: Scout：边缘设备上的开放世界物种识别
translated_abstract: 大型视觉语言模型（VLM）能够实现超越固定类别集合的识别，但其计算需求使其无法在许多边缘设备上运行。云端卸载使这一能力变得可用，但发送每张图像都会消耗稀缺的带宽和通信能量。我们探讨如何在严格的计算、能量和带宽预算内，将VLM的开放世界识别能力带到边缘端。野生动物监测为探索这一问题提供了天然场景，因为红外触发相机（camera traps）会遇到部署时未知的物种。我们提出了Scout，一个自主的开放世界识别系统，它间歇性地调用云端VLM来向紧凑的边缘模型教授新类别。仅需给定部署位置和空场景帧，Scout就能自主地将VLM识别出的每个物种转化为资源高效的边缘模型中持久的、针对特定地点的识别能力，而无需预定义……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: Scout是一个面向边缘设备的自主开放世界物种识别系统，通过间歇性调用云端VLM持续教会轻量边缘模型识别新物种，在计算、能量和带宽严格受限的野生动物监测场景下实现持久的地点自适应识别能力。
en_tdlr: Scout is an autonomous open-world recognition system that intermittently invokes a cloud VLM to teach new species to a compact edge model, enabling persistent site-conditioned recognition for wildlife monitoring within tight compute, energy, and bandwidth budgets.
